proof:
For $F_p\ne Q$, choose a linear functional $u$ on $\operatorname{span}(Q-p)$ that vanishes on $F_p-p$ and is strictly positive on $P\setminus F_p$ after translation by $p$. Such a functional exists because every face of a polytope is exposed. The full objective at a feasible parameter is at least the face objective at its orthogonal projection onto $V_p$, which is at least $E_p$. Conversely, for any feasible face parameter $\alpha$, take $\alpha+t u$ in the full parameter space, identifying $u$ with its representing vector. The face denominators stay fixed, and for large $t$ the other denominators are positive and tend to infinity. Thus the infima agree, while every finite feasible full parameter has a strictly positive contribution from $P\setminus F_p$. If $F_p=Q$, the full problem is the face problem.

In positive face dimension there is a relative ball of radius $r>0$ about $p$ in $F_p$. Positivity of $1+\alpha\cdot(x-p)$ on the ball follows by convexity from positivity on $P_p$. Testing at distance $r$ in the opposite direction to $\alpha$ gives $r\|\alpha\|<1$, taking the ball closed and small enough. Along a sequence of feasible parameters tending to the boundary, some denominator tends to zero and its positive-mass summand tends to infinity. Thus the sublevel set at the value of $\alpha=0$ is compact, and the continuous objective attains a minimum inside its domain. The second directional derivative in any nonzero direction $v\in V_p$ is
$$
N(N+1)\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z L_z(\alpha)^{-N-2}\bigl(v\cdot(z-p)\bigr)^2>0,
$$
since the offsets span $V_p$. This proves uniqueness. In rank zero the sole relative parameter is zero and the same conclusion is immediate.

Stationarity gives $\sum_z e_z(z-p)=0$. Taking its scalar product with $\alpha_p$ gives $\sum_{z\in P_p}e_z L_z(\alpha_p)=\sum_z e_z$. The left side is $E_p$, giving both escort identities. The same identities hold directly on a singleton face.

Every feasible barycentric row is supported on $P_p$. For a proper face this follows by averaging the exposing functional, which is nonnegative and has mean zero. For any feasible face parameter $\alpha$, the constraints give $\sum_{z\in P_p}\lambda_z L_z(\alpha)=1$. Hölder's inequality with exponents $N+1$ and $(N+1)/N$ therefore gives
$$
\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z^{1/(N+1)}\lambda_z^s
=\sum_{z\in P_p}(m_z L_z(\alpha)^{-N})^{1/(N+1)}(\lambda_z L_z(\alpha))^s
\le \left(\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z L_z(\alpha)^{-N}\right)^{1/(N+1)}.
$$
At $\alpha_p$ the row $e/E_p$ is feasible, and its $\lambda_z L_z(\alpha_p)$ are proportional to $m_z L_z(\alpha_p)^{-N}$. This gives equality. The objective before the outer power is strictly concave on the barycentric polytope, so its maximizer is unique. Mixing the maximizing rows at two points produces a feasible row at their affine combination. Concavity of that same objective proves concavity of $E_p^{1/(N+1)}$. Substituting $m_z=M\pi_z$ and $1-s=1/(N+1)$ proves the stated Rényi identity.

For the fiber conclusion, each centroid $g_z$ is interior to its positive-volume convex fiber. In the Minkowski combination use a ball about one centroid with $\lambda_z>0$ and use the centroids themselves at the other positions. This gives a positive-radius ball around $\sum_z\lambda_z g_z$ inside $K_p$.
statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in an affine Euclidean space, with masses $m_z>0$ for $z\in P$, and put $Q=\operatorname{conv} P$ and $M=\sum_{z\in P}m_z$. Fix $N>0$ and $p\in Q$. Let $F_p$ be the unique face of $Q$ with $p\in\operatorname{relint} F_p$, and write $P_p=P\cap F_p$ and $V_p=\operatorname{span}(F_p-p)$. Set
$$
L_z(\alpha)=1+\alpha\cdot(z-p),\qquad
E_p=\inf_{\substack{\alpha\in V_p\\L_z(\alpha)>0\ (z\in P_p)}}\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z L_z(\alpha)^{-N}.
$$

The infimum is attained at a unique $\alpha_p$. Its value is also the infimum of the analogous sum over $P$ with $\alpha\in\operatorname{span}(Q-p)$ and all denominators positive. This latter infimum is attained exactly when $F_p=Q$. In particular a singleton face $F_p=\{p\}$ gives $E_p=m_p$.

Let $e_z=m_zL_z(\alpha_p)^{-N-1}$ on $P_p$, and $e_z=0$ off $P_p$. Then $\sum_{z\in P}e_z=E_p$ and $\sum_{z\in P}e_z z=E_p p$. With $s=N/(N+1)$,
$$
E_p=\max_{\substack{\lambda_z\ge0,\ \sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z=1\\\sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z z=p}}
\left(\sum_{z\in P}m_z^{1/(N+1)}\lambda_z^s\right)^{N+1},
$$
and the unique maximizer is $\lambda_z=e_z/E_p$. In particular $E_p^{1/(N+1)}$ is concave on $Q$. If $\pi_z=m_z/M$ and $D_s(\lambda\Vert\pi)=(s-1)^{-1}\log\sum_z\lambda_z^s\pi_z^{1-s}$, then $E_p/M=\exp(-\min_\lambda D_s(\lambda\Vert\pi))$, over the same constraint set.

If $p\in P$ and $m_z$ are volumes of positive-volume compact convex $d$-fibers $K_z$ with centroids $g_z$, assume $\sum_z\lambda_z K_z\subseteq K_p$ for the displayed maximizing row (as for fibers of a convex body). Then $\sum_z\lambda_z g_z\in\operatorname{int}K_p$.
